answer:
The **Chapter House at Westminster Abbey** was built under **King Henry III** during the period approximately **1246–1255**.

Henry III was crowned twice:

1. **First Coronation:** **October 28, 1216**, at Gloucester Abbey  
   - This was an emergency/hurried ceremony because his father King John died only 9 days earlier
   - He was just 9 years old at the time
   - Due to the circumstances (King John had lost the crown in The Wash), his mother used a gold diadem/corolla instead of the royal crown

2. **Second/Official Coronation:** **May 17, 1220**, at Westminster Abbey  
   - This was the formal, traditional coronation ceremony
   - Occurred approximately 4 years after the first
   - Took place after political stability had been restored following the Barons' War
   - Had papal permission and full ceremonial requirements

If you're looking for his **official/formal coronation date**, it would be **May 17, 1220**. However, since either event marks his crowning while under whom the Chapter House was constructed, both dates could technically apply depending on which event you consider "the crowning."
